newsitem.title: USA: Siemens unit to sell Pocket GSM supplies.
newsitem.headline: Siemens unit to sell Pocket GSM supplies.

text.p: Siemens Stromberg-Carlson said on Wednesday it would sell Pocket Communications Inc GSM equipment and services worth $250 million over the next three years, for an undisclosed sum.
The equipment included mobile switching systems, base stations, base station controllers and micro base stations, Siemens said in a statement.
Pocket Communications, a start-up company, won 43 wireless personal communications services (PCS) licenses in the recent Federal Communications Commission auction, it said.
The first installations were planned for mid-1997 in the Detroit, Mich. area, Siemens said.
Siemens Stromberg-Carlson, a subsidiary of German-based Siemens AG, provided telecommunications equipment to the public network service providers in North America.
Siemens would deploy its D1900 product line, a PCS 1900 technology based on the GSM world standard.

Pocket Communications is based in Washington D.C. and would offer consumers and businesses an array of wireless telecommunications services, including local, long distance, information, messaging, data and fax transmission.
